headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if Devin ingests awesome-prompts content as instructions; Devin’s broad write/network powers amplify the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt-writing repository, so if Devin ingests its content through files, MCP, or copied prompts, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair has no documented shared channel, but Devin can use MCP, files, and browser-based workflows, while awesome-prompts is a content source that could be treated as trusted instructions.
conditions: IF Devin imports prompt text from awesome-prompts into an MCP tool, file, or browser workflow without provenance checks, injection becomes actionable.
IF the repository content is manually copied into Devin’s task context, prompt hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Require provenance labels on imported prompt text.
Strip executable instructions from copied prompt libraries.
Use a separate read-only review step before Devin consumes prompt content.
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted prompt repositories.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not itself a leakage source. Devin, however, reads files and has broad network egress plus integrations, so if sensitive workspace content is placed into the pair, Devin can transmit it outward. The risk is limited because the source agent does not handle sensitive data by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are copied into Devin’s cloud workspace, Devin can exfiltrate them via network egress or integrations.
IF awesome-prompts is used as a source of internal prompts containing secrets, those secrets can flow into Devin outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of prompt libraries.
Use redacted copies of any internal prompts.
Restrict Devin integrations for sensitive tasks.
Review outbound destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Devin egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot directly contend for mutable resources. Devin can write files, modify git state, and use shared integrations, but the pair lacks a shared writable surface in the profiles. The main conflict path is indirect and requires external orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an operator maps awesome-prompts output into the same repo or workspace Devin edits, write conflicts can occur.
IF both are pointed at the same GitHub branch through integrations, Devin can race with imported prompt artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories.
Freeze prompt-library updates during Devin runs.
Use PR review before merging Devin changes.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared git targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository, so Devin may treat its content as authoritative task guidance if imported. Devin is autonomous and can act on browser, shell, and integration outputs, so a bad prompt can cascade into incorrect code or issue actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Devin uses awesome-prompts content as a task template without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Devin is allowed to commit or message based on imported prompt instructions, errors can propagate to shared systems.
mitigations: Require human review of imported prompts.
Use a verification step before Devin acts on generated plans.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for prompt-derived tasks.
Log source provenance for every imported instruction.
requires-engineering: add policy gates before external actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is explicitly assigned to awesome-prompts, while Devin handles source code, issue trackers, chat, and docs with cloud integrations. That creates a modest compliance mismatch risk if regulated content is introduced, but the profiles do not show PHI or residency-specific data by default. The other agent is not cited for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into Devin’s integrations, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to imported prompt content, Devin’s cloud workspace must honor them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings for Devin integrations.
Use anonymized examples in prompt libraries.
Document data-handling rules for shared tasks.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
